Explain the business logic of this DirXML policy.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Get connection-dn from search-attr of matching query</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-operation mode="nocase" op="equal">query</if-operation>
											<if-xpath op="true">search-attr[@attr-name='connection-dn']</if-xpath>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-op-property name="connection-dn">
											<arg-string>
												<token-xpath expression="search-attr[@attr-name='connection-dn']" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-op-property>
										<do-strip-xpath expression="search-attr[@name='connection-dn']" />
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule processes query operations to extract a 'connection-dn' value from search attributes. When a query operation contains a search-attr element with attr-name='connection-dn', the rule sets an operation property named 'connection-dn' with that value, then strips the search attribute from the document. Note: there's an inconsistency in the XPath expressions - the condition checks for @attr-name while the strip action checks for @name.

content.text: Create a NetIQ DirXML policy rule that standardizes and synchronizes fax numbers for User objects on modify events. Parse fax numbers to extract ISD code (after '+'), area code (within parentheses), phone number (after area code), and extension (after ' x'). If no international code exists, prepend '+1 '. If the format is +X xxx-xxx-xxxx, reformat to +X (xxx) xxx-xxxx. Store parsed components in local variables with LV-IDV-FaxNumber prefix and reformat the Facsimile Telephone Number attribute with the standardized value.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Synchronize workday Facsimile Telephone Number - if different for modify event</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-operation mode="nocase" op="equal">modify</if-operation>
											<if-op-attr name="Facsimile Telephone Number" op="changing" />
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" scope="policy">
											<arg-string>
												<token-op-attr name="Facsimile Telephone Number" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-xpath op="true">contains($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, '+')</if-xpath>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-ISDCodeTemp" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-after($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, '+')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-ISDCode" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-before($LV-IDV-FaxNumber-ISDCodeTemp,' (')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions />
										</do-if>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-xpath op="true">contains($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, ' (')</if-xpath>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-AreaCodeTemp" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-after($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, ' (')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-AreaCode" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-before($LV-IDV-FaxNumber-AreaCodeTemp,')')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions />
										</do-if>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-xpath op="true">contains($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, ' x')</if-xpath>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-PhoneTemp" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-after($LV-IDV-FaxNumber,') ')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-Phone" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-before($LV-IDv-FaxNumber-PhoneTemp,' x')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-Ext" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-after($LV-IDV-FaxNumber-PhoneTemp,' x')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-Phone" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="substring-after($LV-IDV-FaxNumber,') ')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
											</arg-actions>
										</do-if>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-xpath op="true">string-length($LV-IDV-FaxNumber) > 1</if-xpath>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-if>
													<arg-conditions>
														<and>
															<if-local-variable mode="regex" name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" op="not-equal">^\+[0-9]+\s.*$</if-local-variable>
														</and>
													</arg-conditions>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">+1 </token-text>
																<token-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-ISDCode" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">1</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
													</arg-actions>
													<arg-actions />
												</do-if>
												<do-if>
													<arg-conditions>
														<and>
															<if-xpath op="not-true">contains($LV-IDV-FaxNumber, ' (')</if-xpath>
															<if-local-variable mode="regex" name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" op="equal">^\+[0-9]+\s[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}.*$</if-local-variable>
														</and>
													</arg-conditions>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber-AreaCode" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-replace-all regex="^(\+[0-9]+\s)([0-9]{3})-([0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}).*$" replace-with="$2">
																	<token-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" />
																</token-replace-all>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-replace-all regex="^(\+[0-9]+\s)([0-9]{3})-([0-9]{3}-[0-9]{4}.*)$" replace-with="$1($2) $3">
																	<token-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" />
																</token-replace-all>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
													</arg-actions>
													<arg-actions />
												</do-if>
												<do-reformat-op-attr name="Facsimile Telephone Number">
													<arg-value>
														<token-local-variable name="LV-IDV-FaxNumber" />
													</arg-value>
												</do-reformat-op-attr>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions />
										</do-if>
									</actions>
								</rule>

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Rename "LOCKUSER" attribute to "ISLocked" attribute for IG Query</description>
									<conditions>
										<or>
											<if-operation mode="nocase" op="equal">query</if-operation>
										</or>
										<or>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">US</if-class-name>
										</or>
										<or>
											<if-op-property mode="nocase" name="ig-account-collection-query" op="equal">true</if-op-property>
										</or>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-rename-op-attr dest-name="ISLOCKED:LOCAL_LOCK" src-name="LOCKUSER" />
									</actions>
								</rule>

This DirXML rule executes during query operations on User (US) objects initiated by Identity Governance account collection queries. It renames the 'LOCKUSER' attribute to 'ISLOCKED:LOCAL_LOCK' in the query operation, allowing Identity Governance to use a different attribute name convention than what exists in the connected system. The three OR conditions ensure this only applies to: (1) query operations, (2) User class objects, and (3) operations marked as Identity Governance account collection queries via the operation property.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Set uniqueID if unavailable</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">This rule will set uniqueID with CN if uniqueID is not available</comment>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-operation mode="nocase" op="equal">add</if-operation>
											<if-attr name="uniqueID" op="not-available" />
											<if-attr name="CN" op="available" />
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-clone-op-attr dest-name="uniqueID" src-name="CN" />
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule triggers during User object additions when the 'uniqueID' attribute is missing but 'CN' (Common Name) is present. It copies the CN value to uniqueID to ensure every user has a unique identifier, using CN as the fallback source when uniqueID isn't provided.

Fix the syntax errors in this DirXML policy based on the DTD.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>RACFAccount entitlement: Match existing accounts if RACFAccount Onboarding enabled</description>
	<comment xml:space="preserve">If the RACFAccount GCV is set to true, this policy prevents the onboarding of user accounts from RACF unless the RACFAccount AND RACFAccount.onboard GCV is also set to true.</comment>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
			<if-op-property mode="nocase" name="attempt-to-match" op="equal">true</if-op-property>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<or>
				<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.AllowUserAdd" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
			</or>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-set-op-property name="attempt-to-match">
			<arg-string>
				<token-text xml:space="preserve">false</token-text>
			</arg-string>
		</do-set-op-property>
	</actions>
</rule>

The broken XML violates the DirXML DTD by nesting an <or> element inside an <and> element with only one child condition. According to the DTD, logical operators like <or> require at least two child conditions to be valid. The original XML had three separate <and> blocks at the same level within <conditions>, which creates an implicit OR relationship between them. The fix removes the invalid nested <or> and restores the original structure with three parallel <and> conditions. In DirXML, multiple condition blocks at the same level under <conditions> are evaluated with OR logic, so if any of the three <and> blocks evaluates to true, the rule actions will execute.

content.text:
Fix the syntax errors in this DirXML policy based on the DTD.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
  <description>Check for Entitlement</description>
  <comment xml:space="preserve">If Entitlements are enabled then check for the bbAccount Entitlement on new users.  If not found then veto.</comment>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-op-property mode="nocase" name="BBObjectType" op="equal">DirXML-BB-Person</if-op-property>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="use_entitlements" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-entitlement name="bbAccount" op="not-available" />
      <if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-veto />
  </actions>
</rule>

The broken XML adds an extra condition '<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>' within the <and> block. According to NetIQ DirXML DTD rules, <if-class-name> elements must appear before other conditional elements like <if-op-property>, <if-global-variable>, and <if-entitlement> within boolean operators. The correct structure requires reordering conditions with <if-class-name> first:

Corrected XML:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
  <description>Check for Entitlement</description>
  <comment xml:space="preserve">If Entitlements are enabled then check for the bbAccount Entitlement on new users.  If not found then veto.</comment>
  <conditions>
    <and>
      <if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
      <if-op-property mode="nocase" name="BBObjectType" op="equal">DirXML-BB-Person</if-op-property>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="use_entitlements" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-entitlement name="bbAccount" op="not-available" />
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-veto />
  </actions>
</rule>

      <if-op-property mode="nocase" name="attempt-to-match" op="equal">true</if-op-property>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.UserAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
    </and>
    <and>
      <if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
      <if-op-property mode="nocase" name="attempt-to-match" op="equal">true</if-op-property>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.UserAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.AllowUserAdd" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
      <if-op-attr mode="nocase" name="Login Disabled" op="equal">true</if-op-attr>
    </and>
  </conditions>
  <actions>
    <do-set-op-property name="attempt-to-match">
      <arg-string>
        <token-text xml:space="preserve">false</token-text>
      </arg-string>
    </do-set-op-property>
  </actions>
</rule>

The original XML violates the NetIQ DirXML DTD by having three separate <and> condition blocks at the same level within <conditions>, which creates an implicit OR relationship. However, the third <and> block duplicates several conditions from the second block (checking UserAccount=true, onboarding=true, and attempt-to-match=true) while adding the 'Login Disabled' check. This is logically redundant. The corrected XML merges the second and third condition blocks: since both check for UserAccount enabled AND onboarding enabled AND attempt-to-match true, and differ only in checking either 'AllowUserAdd != true' OR 'Login Disabled = true', these two checks can be combined in a single <and> block. The fix consolidates the logic while maintaining the same functional behavior: the rule triggers when UserAccount entitlement is enabled with either onboarding disabled (first block) OR when onboarding is enabled but either AllowUserAdd is false or the account is disabled (merged second block).

This ensures operation-data is properly populated for downstream Workday operations with correct worker identification and regional context.

</comment>

														</token-parse-dn>

												</token-src-attr>
											</arg-string>

										<do-set-local-variable name="grpObj" scope="policy">
											<arg-node-set>
												<token-query class-name="DirXML-Entitlement" datastore="src">
													<arg-dn>
														<token-global-variable name="dirxml.auto.driverdn" />
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">\</token-text>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Group</token-text>
													</arg-dn>
												</token-query>

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Break if not an appropriate event or a non-placeable class</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="gcv.NOVLGGLEORGU.googlePlacementOption" op="equal">none</if-global-variable>
										</and>
										<and>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="not-equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="not-equal">Organizational Unit</if-class-name>
											<if-operation mode="case" op="not-equal">move</if-operation>
											<if-xml-attr mode="nocase" name="from-merge" op="not-equal">true</if-xml-attr>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-break />
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule implements a two-part check to determine whether to break processing. It breaks if EITHER: (1) the global variable 'gcv.NOVLGGLEORGU.googlePlacementOption' equals 'none', OR (2) ALL of the following conditions are true: the class is not 'User', the class is not 'Organizational Unit', the operation is not 'move', and the from-merge attribute is not 'true'. In summary, it filters out events that should not be processed based on placement settings or when the event doesn't involve placeable classes (User/OU) in appropriate contexts (move operations or merge scenarios).

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Strip association-ref attribute from User object 'homeMDB' values</description>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-class-name mode="regex" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.Exchange.onboard" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-strip-xpath expression="*[@attr-name="homeMDB"]/descendant::value/@*" />
		<do-set-local-variable name="invalid-element">
			<invalid-element/>
		</do-set-local-variable>
	</actions>
</rule>

The broken XML includes an invalid element '<invalid-element/>' within a do-set-local-variable action. According to the DirXML DTD, do-set-local-variable expects specific child elements like <token>, <arg-value>, or <xpath>, but '<invalid-element/>' is not a valid child element. The fix is to remove the entire do-set-local-variable action block, restoring the XML to its original valid state with only the do-strip-xpath action that performs the intended functionality.

												<do-set-xml-attr expression="./following-sibling::instance[@src-dn = $current-node]/attr[last()]" name="attr-name">
													<arg-string>

This rule intercepts a tagged identity query response for GoogleAccount entitlements. When triggered (by a local variable flag, an 'instance' operation, and a driver identification class), it transforms the response into one or more GoogleAccount instances. It first converts the current instance to a GoogleAccount for the primary domain (from global variable gcv.NOVLGGLEBCFG.domainName), setting display name, description, and value attributes. It then iterates through subdomain names (from gcv.NOVLGGLEBCFG.subDomainNames) and creates additional GoogleAccount instances for each subdomain with similar attributes. This effectively presents available Google Apps accounts across multiple domains as entitlement options.

<rule>

Fix the syntax errors in this DirXML policy based on the DTD.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Job Profile: Create Rename Event</description>
	<comment xml:space="preserve">If the naming attribute specified by a GCV is changing, process the current event and then send a rename afterward.</comment>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">WDJobProfile</if-class-name>
			<if-operation mode="nocase" op="equal">modify</if-operation>
			<if-global-variable mode="regex" name="gvJobProfileNameMappingAttr" op="equal">.+</if-global-variable>
			<if-op-attr name="~gvJobProfileNameMappingAttr~" op="changing" />
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-rename-dest-object class-name="WDJobProfile">
			<arg-string>
				<token-attr name="~gvJobProfileNameMappingAttr~" />
			</arg-string>
		</do-rename-dest-object>
	</actions>
</rule>

The DTD violation occurs because the 'when' attribute is missing from the <do-rename-dest-object> element. According to the NetIQ DirXML DTD, the 'when' attribute is required for this action element and must specify either 'before' or 'after' to indicate when the rename should occur relative to the current operation. The corrected XML removes the when="after" attribute, which creates an invalid document. To fix this and make it valid again, the 'when' attribute must be restored: <do-rename-dest-object class-name="WDJobProfile" when="after">.

content.text: Create a NetIQ DirXML rule that intercepts query-driver-ident status events with UserAccountEntitlementQuery operation data, retrieves ConnectedSystemName from global variables, constructs a synthetic PosixAccount instance with display name, description, and value attributes all populated with the system name, and strips empty attribute elements

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Intercept PosixAccount (tagged identity query) query status</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-xpath op="true">../status[@event-id='query-driver-ident']/operation-data/@UserAccountEntitlementQuery</if-xpath>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-local-variable name="ConnectedSystemName" scope="policy">
											<arg-string>
												<token-global-variable name="ConnectedSystemName" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-trace-message>
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">found Linux and Unix system name: </token-text>
												<token-local-variable name="ConnectedSystemName" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-trace-message>
										<do-append-xml-element expression=".." name="instance" />
										<do-set-xml-attr expression="../instance[last()]" name="class-name">
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">PosixAccount</token-text>
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-xml-attr>
										<do-set-xml-attr expression="../instance[last()]" name="src-dn">
											<arg-string>
												<token-local-variable name="ConnectedSystemName" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-xml-attr>

content.text:
Fix the syntax errors in this DirXML policy based on the DTD.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Only allow resource objects of type Entitlement Configuration (text/vnd.novell.idm.entitlementConfiguration+xml)</description>
	<comment xml:space="preserve">For DirXML-Resources require DirXML-ContentType=text/vnd.novell.idm.entitlementConfiguration+xml</comment>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">DirXML-Resource</if-class-name>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-veto-if-op-attr-not-available name="DirXML-ContentType" />
		<do-if>
			<arg-conditions>
				<and>
					<if-op-attr mode="nocase" name="DirXML-ContentType" op="not-equal">text/vnd.novell.idm.entitlementConfiguration+xml</if-op-attr>
				</and>
			</arg-conditions>
			<arg-actions>
				<do-veto />
			</arg-actions>
		</do-if>
	</actions>
</rule>

The original XML violates the DTD by having an empty <arg-actions /> element as the else-clause of the <do-if> statement. According to the DirXML DTD, when a <do-if> element is present, it requires exactly two <arg-actions> children - one for the 'then' branch and one for the 'else' branch. However, the 'else' branch can be truly empty (no action elements inside), but it must still be a proper container element with opening and closing tags. The corrected version removes the self-closing empty <arg-actions /> tag and instead uses <arg-actions></arg-actions> or simply omits the else clause entirely by having only one <arg-actions> element when no else-logic is needed. In this fix, I removed the empty else clause completely since no action is needed when the condition is false.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Block empty modify operations</description>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-operation op="equal">modify</if-operation>
			<if-xpath op="not-true">modify-attr</if-xpath>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-veto>
			<arg-string>Invalid content inside do-veto</arg-string>
		</do-veto>
	</actions>
</rule>

The DTD violation was introduced by adding an <arg-string> child element inside the <do-veto> element. According to the NetIQ DirXML schema, <do-veto> is an empty element that only accepts <arg-*> attributes for the veto message, not child elements. The corrected XML removes the invalid child element:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Block empty modify operations</description>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-operation op="equal">modify</if-operation>
			<if-xpath op="not-true">modify-attr</if-xpath>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-veto/>
	</actions>
</rule>

Alternatively, if a veto message is desired, it should be specified as an attribute:
<do-veto><arg-string><token-text xml:space="preserve">Empty modify operation blocked</token-text></arg-string></do-veto>

<rule>
									<description>Set gidNumber using custom LUM Linux/UNIX Config Object</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-class-name op="equal">Group</if-class-name>
											<if-src-attr name="gidNumber" op="not-available" />
											<if-global-variable name="ModifyGroups" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="UseLUMForUIDGID" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
										</and>
										
										<and>
											<if-class-name op="equal">Group</if-class-name>
											<if-global-variable name="ReplaceValues" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="ModifyGroups" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="UseLUMForUIDGID" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-local-variable name="searchBase">
											<arg-string>
												<token-global-variable name="GIDInUseSearchSubtree" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-local-variable name="DriverDN">
											<arg-string>
												<token-global-variable name="DriverDN" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-local-variable name="driverShimInstance">
											<arg-object>
												<token-xpath expression="NxSettingsInstance:getInstance($DriverDN)" />
											</arg-object>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-local-variable name="UnixConfigObject">
											<arg-string>
												<token-global-variable name="LUMUnixConfig" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-src-attr-value name="gidNumber">
											<arg-value type="string">
												<token-xpath expression="driverShim:getNextIDFromUnixConfig($driverShimInstance,$UnixConfigObject, "gid", $searchBase)" />
											</arg-value>
										</do-set-src-attr-value>
										<do-add-src-attr-value name="Object Class">
											<arg-value type="string">
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">posixGroup</token-text>
											</arg-value>
										</do-add-src-attr-value>
										<do-add-src-attr-value name="Object Class">
											<arg-value type="string">
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">uamPosixGroup</token-text>
											</arg-value>
										</do-add-src-attr-value>
										<do-add-association>
											<arg-association>
												<token-src-attr name="GUID" />
											</arg-association>
										</do-add-association>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This DirXML rule sets the gidNumber attribute for Group objects using a custom LUM (Linux User Management) Unix Config Object. It triggers under two conditions: (1) when a Group lacks a gidNumber and ModifyGroups/UseLUMForUIDGID are enabled, or (2) when ReplaceValues, ModifyGroups, and UseLUMForUIDGID are all enabled. The rule retrieves the next available GID from a Unix Config object using a driver shim, adds posixGroup and uamPosixGroup object classes, and establishes an association using the GUID attribute.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>User RACFAccount Entitlement change (Delete Option)</description>
									<comment>The User RACFAccount Entitlement grants the user an enabled account in the connected system. Revoking the entitlement will disable or delete the user account depending on the value you select for the 'When account entitlement revoked' global variable. This rule executes when the entitlement is changing and you have selected the delete option.</comment>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">delete</if-global-variable>
											<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-operation mode="regex" op="equal">add|modify</if-operation>
											<if-entitlement name="RACFAccount" op="changing" />
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-for-each>
											<arg-node-set>
												<token-removed-entitlement name="RACFAccount" />
											</arg-node-set>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-op-property name="accountAction">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">accountDeleteByEntitlementRevoke</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="sourceDN">
													<arg-string>
														<token-src-dn />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="association">
													<arg-string>
														<token-association />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="guid">
													<arg-string>
														<token-src-attr name="GUID" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="objectClass">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">User</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-break />
											</arg-actions>
										</do-for-each>
										<do-for-each>
											<arg-node-set>
												<token-added-entitlement name="RACFAccount" />
											</arg-node-set>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-op-property name="accountAction">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">accountCreateByEntitlementGrant</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="sourceDN">
													<arg-string>
														<token-src-dn />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="association">
													<arg-string>
														<token-association />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="guid">
													<arg-string>
														<token-src-attr name="GUID" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
												<do-set-op-property name="objectClass">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">User</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
											</arg-actions>
										</do-for-each>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This DirXML policy rule handles User RACFAccount entitlement changes when the removal option is set to 'delete'. It monitors User class objects during add or modify operations where the RACFAccount entitlement is changing. When the entitlement is revoked, it sets operation properties to delete the account (accountAction='accountDeleteByEntitlementRevoke') and breaks from the loop. When the entitlement is granted, it sets properties to create the account (accountAction='accountCreateByEntitlementGrant'). Both scenarios capture source DN, association, GUID, and object class for processing.

This transforms a date/time format into a compact numeric string suitable for IDV attribute format requirements.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>User Account Entitlement change</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">The User Account Entitlement grants the user an enabled account in SAP. Revoking the entitlement will disable or delete the account depending on the value you select for the 'When account entitlement revoked' global variable. This rule executes when the entitlement is changing and you have selected the delete option.</comment>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.UserAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>

									</conditions>

											<arg-conditions>
												<and>

												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>

													</arg-node-set>
													<arg-actions>

															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="dvn" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="removed-lsname" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">-clsname</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="removed-clsname" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="$dvn$" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="dvn" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="removed-lsname" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">-ctype</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="removed-ctype" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="$dvn$" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="dvn" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="removed-lsname" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">-llo</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="removed-llo" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="$dvn$" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-if>

																	<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="removed-ctype" op="not-equal">cua-child</if-local-variable>
																	<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="removed-lsname" op="equal">$lsname$</if-local-variable>
																</and>
															</arg-conditions>
															<arg-actions>
																<do-trace-message>
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">Revoking UserAccount entitlement for object </token-text>
																		<token-src-name />
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve"> and logical system </token-text>
																		<token-local-variable name="removed-lsname" />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-trace-message>
																<do-if>
																	<arg-conditions>
																		<and>
																			<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">delete</if-global-variable>
																		</and>
																	</arg-conditions>
																	<arg-actions>
																		<do-trace-message>
																			<arg-string>
																				<token-text xml:space="preserve">Deleting object </token-text>
																				<token-src-name />
																				<token-text xml:space="preserve"> from logical system </token-text>
																				<token-local-variable name="removed-lsname" />
																			</arg-string>
																		</do-trace-message>
																		<do-delete-dest-object when="after" />
																		<do-remove-association when="after">

content.text: Create a DirXML rule that intercepts and suppresses SCIM driver identification query responses tagged with 'query-driver-ident' event-id and UserAccountEntitlementQuery operation data by stripping the entire document when the operation is 'instance' and class is '__driver_identification_class__'

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Intercept SCIM System (tagged identity query) query response</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-operation mode="case" op="equal">instance</if-operation>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">__driver_identification_class__</if-class-name>
											<if-xpath op="true">//status[@event-id='query-driver-ident']/operation-data/@UserAccountEntitlementQuery</if-xpath>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-strip-xpath expression="." />
									</actions>
								</rule>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Intercept outbound queries for ExternalIdentifier</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">ExternalIdentifier</if-class-name>
											<if-operation mode="regex" op="equal">query|query-ex</if-operation>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-xml-attr expression="." name="event-id">
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">query-driver-ident</token-text>
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-xml-attr>
										<do-strip-xpath expression="@class-name" />
										<do-set-xml-attr expression="." name="scope">
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">entry</token-text>
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-xml-attr>
										<do-strip-xpath expression="search-class" />
										<do-append-xml-element expression="." name="search-class" />
										<do-set-xml-attr expression="search-class[last()]" name="class-name">
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">__driver_identification_class__</token-text>
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-xml-attr>
										<do-strip-xpath expression="read-attr" />
										<do-append-xml-element expression="." name="read-attr" />
										<do-set-op-property name="ExternalIdentifierEntitlementQuery">
											<arg-string>
												<token-dest-dn />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-op-property>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule intercepts outbound queries (query or query-ex operations) targeting the ExternalIdentifier class. When triggered, it modifies the query document by: setting the event-id to 'query-driver-ident', removing the class-name attribute, setting scope to 'entry', removing existing search-class elements, appending a new search-class element with class-name '__driver_identification_class__', removing all read-attr elements, appending a new empty read-attr element, and finally setting an operation property 'ExternalIdentifierEntitlementQuery' with the destination DN value. This effectively transforms an ExternalIdentifier query into a driver identification query.

											</arg-string>

After removal, it sets an XML attribute 'association-ref' on the last remove-value element to maintain the association reference. This effectively re-enables a disabled Notes user by removing them from a 'Deny Access' group when their eDirectory login is enabled.

This rule strips the 'Group Membership' attribute from User objects during add or modify operations when both Account and Group entitlements are enabled. It ensures that group membership is managed exclusively through entitlement grants rather than direct attribute manipulation. This DirXML rule handles Group operations (delete, move, rename, add) during entitlement onboarding. It first validates the operation is on a Group class with entitlement onboarding enabled. The rule retrieves admin credentials, queries the entitlement object, and converts DN formats. For move/rename/delete operations, it refreshes group assignment values, builds operation-data XML with entitlement-assignments containing group metadata (ID, resource, holders), serializes and base64-encodes the payload, then reconciles group member permissions via a custom function. For add operations, it refreshes the code map for the group entitlement. The rule uses extensive XPath queries, DN parsing, table lookups for resource mapping, and iterates through group members to build holder elements.

This policy rule handles role entitlement assignments and revocations for User objects during modify operations. When the global variable 'drv.entitlement.Role' is set to true and a User's Role entitlement is changing, the rule performs two operations: First, it iterates through removed role entitlements, extracts the role ID from entitlement parameters, and removes the user's DN from the corresponding DirectoryRole object's members attribute. This maintains bidirectional synchronization between user role entitlements and DirectoryRole membership lists.

content.text: Create a NetIQ DirXML rule that responds to entitlement query status operations by parsing event-id 'ENTITLEMENT:<name>', retrieving and decoding base64 XML from '<name>_Values' resource object's DirXML-Data attribute, then constructing instance elements with DisplayName and Description attributes for each value found in the decoded XML structure

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Build reply to Entitlement Query</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">This policy builds a reply to a stubbed entitlement query generated in sub-ctp-EntitlementQueryHandler. It depends on the well-known format "ENTITLEMENT:<name>" in the event-id of a status operation, and populates value instances from the well-known "<name>_Values" resource objects created to hold entitlement values.</comment>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-operation mode="case" op="equal">status</if-operation>
											<if-xml-attr mode="nocase" name="level" op="equal">success</if-xml-attr>
											<if-xml-attr mode="regex" name="event-id" op="equal">^(ENTITLEMENT:).*$</if-xml-attr>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										
										<do-set-local-variable name="eventIdNodes" scope="policy">
											<arg-node-set>
												<token-split delimiter=":">
													<token-xpath expression="$current-op/@event-id" />
												</token-split>
											</arg-node-set>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-local-variable name="entFlag" scope="policy">
											<arg-string>
												<token-xpath expression="$eventIdNodes[1]" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="entFlag" op="equal">ENTITLEMENT</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-xml-attr expression="$current-op" name="level">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">success</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-xml-attr>
												<do-strip-xpath expression="./description" />
												<do-append-xml-element expression="." name="description" />
												<do-append-xml-text expression="./description">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Successfully processed Entitlement Values</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-append-xml-text>
												<do-set-local-variable name="valuesObj" scope="policy">
													<arg-node-set>
														<token-query class-name="DirXML-Resource" datastore="dest" scope="entry">
															<arg-dn>
																<token-global-variable name="dirxml.auto.driverdn" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">\</token-text>
																<token-xpath expression="$eventIdNodes[2]" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">_Values</token-text>
															</arg-dn>
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">DirXML-Data</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</token-query>
													</arg-node-set>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												
												<do-set-local-variable name="valuesXmlStr" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-base64-decode charset="UTF-8">
															<token-xpath expression="$valuesObj/attr[@attr-name='DirXML-Data']/value[1]/text()" />
														</token-base64-decode>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-set-local-variable name="valuesXml" scope="policy">
													<arg-node-set>
														<token-xml-parse>
															<token-local-variable name="valuesXmlStr" />
														</token-xml-parse>
													</arg-node-set>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-for-each>
													<arg-node-set>
														<token-xpath expression="$valuesXml/values/value" />
													</arg-node-set>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-trace-message>
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">value line: </token-text>
																<token-xpath expression="$current-node/text()" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-trace-message>
														<do-append-xml-element expression="$current-op/.." name="instance" />
														<do-set-xml-attr expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]" name="class-name">
															<arg-string>
																<token-xpath expression="$eventIdNodes[2]" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-xml-attr>
														<do-set-xml-attr expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]" name="src-dn">
															<arg-string>
																<token-xpath expression="$current-node/text()" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-xml-attr>
														<do-append-xml-element expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]" name="association" />
														<do-append-xml-text expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]/association">
															<arg-string>

															</arg-string>
														</do-append-xml-text>
														<do-append-xml-element expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]" name="attr" />
														<do-set-xml-attr expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]/attr[last()]" name="attr-name">
															<arg-string>

															</arg-string>
														</do-set-xml-attr>
														<do-append-xml-element expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]/attr[last()]" name="value" />
														<do-append-xml-text expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]/attr[last()]/value">
															<arg-string>

															</arg-string>
														</do-append-xml-text>
														<do-append-xml-element expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]" name="attr" />
														<do-set-xml-attr expression="$current-op/../instance[last()]/attr[last()]" name="attr-name">
															<arg-string>

This rule handles error recovery for unassociated objects that have existing UserAccount entitlements. It detects objects that previously failed fanout operations and re-attempts to fanout the event to the appropriate logical systems. The rule first checks if the object is unassociated, has UserAccount entitlements, and those entitlements are not currently changing. It then iterates through each UserAccount entitlement to identify which logical systems need fanout. For each logical system (except the primary one and child CUA types), it creates new add commands with the appropriate attributes from the driver filter. The rule also handles entitlement references, stripping those that don't belong to the target logical system. Finally, it cleans up empty attribute operations and the event itself if no modifications remain.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Strip Login Disabled from operation (RACFAccount Entitlement but NO Onboarding)</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">If entitlements control whether the account in the application is enabled or disabled (as in the Disable Option), we'll disregard changes to Login Disabled.
If RACFAccount onboarding is allowed we will strip the attribute in the pub-ctp-PermissionAttributesCaching policy</comment>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">disable</if-global-variable>
											<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-op-attr name="Login Disabled" op="available" />
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount.onboard" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
										</and>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">disable</if-global-variable>
											<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-op-attr name="Login Disabled" op="available" />
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-strip-op-attr name="Login Disabled" />
									</actions>
								</rule>

This DirXML rule manages the 'Login Disabled' attribute for User objects when RACFAccount entitlements control account enablement. It strips the 'Login Disabled' attribute when: (1) RACFAccount entitlement is active, (2) the removal mode is 'disable', (3) the object is a User, (4) Login Disabled is present in the operation, and (5) onboarding is NOT enabled. The rule checks two different onboarding flags as alternatives - either 'drv.entitlement.RACFAccount.onboard' or 'drv.entitlement.onboarding' must not be true. This prevents conflicts when entitlements manage account status, delegating Login Disabled handling to the pub-ctp-PermissionAttributesCaching policy when onboarding is active.

This NetIQ DirXML rule handles a merge operation for Workday user objects. When the 'wd-Merge' attribute changes to 'True' on a user object, the rule validates that both 'workforceID' and 'wd-WorkerIDType' attributes are present (vetoing if either is missing). It then constructs a query XML element to search for the target user in the identity vault using these identifiers. The rule stores workforce ID and worker type in driver-scoped variables, builds search criteria, and includes driver operation data with workforce information. It also handles an optional effective date for the merge - if 'wd-Merge-effectiveDate' is provided and is in the future, it uses that date; otherwise, it uses the current date. After constructing the query, the rule clears the merge-related attributes and vetoes the current operation, allowing the query to execute separately to find and merge with the target user object.

									<comment>The User RACFAccount Entitlement grants the user an enabled account in the connected system. Revoking the entitlement will disable or delete the user account depending on the value you select for the 'When account entitlement revoked' global variable. This rule executes when the entitlement is changing and you have selected the disable option.</comment>

														<token-text xml:space="preserve">User</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-op-property>
											</arg-actions>
										</do-for-each>

This rule handles the RACFAccount entitlement for User objects when the global configuration specifies that revoking the entitlement should disable (not delete) the account. The rule triggers on add or modify operations when the RACFAccount entitlement is changing. It contains two do-for-each loops: the first processes removed entitlements and sets operation properties to disable the account (accountAction='accountDisableByEntitlementRevoke'), while the second processes added entitlements and sets properties to enable the account (accountAction='accountEnableByEntitlementGrant'). Both loops capture the source DN, association, GUID, and objectClass for downstream processing.

<rule>
									<description>0-0: Fanout associated objects by existing UserAccount Entitlement (error recovery)</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.UserAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
											<if-association op="available" />
											<if-entitlement name="UserAccount" op="not-changing" />
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-set-local-variable name="lsname" scope="policy">
											<arg-string>
												<token-xpath expression="substring-after(substring-before(association/text(), '\USd'),'\')" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-set-local-variable name="fanout" scope="policy">

												<token-text xml:space="preserve">false</token-text>

										</do-set-local-variable>
										<do-for-each>
											<arg-node-set>
												<token-entitlement name="UserAccount" />
											</arg-node-set>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="this.lsname" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														
														<token-xpath expression="es:getEntParamFieldBackwardsCompatible($current-node, 'LIID','LSNAME')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-if>
													<arg-conditions>
														<and>
															<if-xpath op="true">$this.lsname!=$lsname</if-xpath>
															<if-xpath op="true">count($event//node()[@lsname=$this.lsname])=0</if-xpath>
															<if-xpath op="true">count(node()[@lsname=$this.lsname])=0</if-xpath>
															<if-xpath op="true">count($event//association[starts-with(text(), concat('\', $this.lsname))])=0</if-xpath>
															<if-xpath op="true">count(association[starts-with(text(), concat('\', $this.lsname))])=0</if-xpath>
														</and>
													</arg-conditions>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-set-local-variable name="lvTmp" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">0-0: Detected potentially previously failed fanout condition. Preparing to re-fanout event for associated object: </token-text>
																<token-src-name />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve"> to system: </token-text>
																<token-xpath expression="$this.lsname" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-if>
															<arg-conditions>
																<and>
																	<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.proclog.enabled" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
																</and>
															</arg-conditions>
															<arg-actions>
																<do-set-local-variable name="lvFile" scope="policy">
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-xpath expression="es:writeLog($lvLogfile,concat(es:fixLength(' ',18),$lvTmp))" />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-local-variable>
															</arg-actions>
															<arg-actions />
														</do-if>
														<do-set-local-variable name="fanout" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">true</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
													</arg-actions>
													<arg-actions />
												</do-if>
											</arg-actions>
										</do-for-each>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="fanout" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="filter" scope="policy">
													<arg-node-set>
														<token-xml-parse>
															<token-base64-decode charset="UTF-8">
																<token-query class-name="Driver" datastore="src" scope="entry">
																	<arg-dn>
																		<token-global-variable name="dirxml.auto.driverdn" />
																	</arg-dn>
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:ilm:core:1.0:Driver:filters</token-text>
																	</arg-string>
																</token-query>
															</token-base64-decode>
														</token-xml-parse>
													</arg-node-set>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-for-each>
													<arg-node-set>
														<token-entitlement name="UserAccount" />
													</arg-node-set>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-set-local-variable name="granted-lsname" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																
																<token-xpath expression="es:getEntParamFieldBackwardsCompatible($current-node, 'LIID','LSNAME')" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="dvn" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="granted-lsname" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">-clsname</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="granted-clsname" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="$dvn$" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="dvn" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-local-variable name="granted-lsname" />
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">-ctype</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-set-local-variable name="granted-ctype" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>

																	<if-xpath op="true">count(association[starts-with(text(), concat('\', $granted-lsname))])=0</if-xpath>
																</and>
															</arg-conditions>
															<arg-actions>
																<do-set-local-variable name="lvTmp" scope="policy">
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">0-0: Re-attempting to fanout to system: $granted-lsname$</token-text>
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-local-variable>
																<do-if>
																	<arg-conditions>
																		<and>
																			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.proclog.enabled" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
																		</and>
																	</arg-conditions>
																	<arg-actions>

																		<token-class-name />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-local-variable>
																<do-add-dest-object class-name="$class-name$" when="after">
																	<arg-dn>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">fanout</token-text>
																	</arg-dn>
																</do-add-dest-object>
																<do-set-xml-attr expression="../add[last()]/operation-data" name="lsname">
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-local-variable name="granted-lsname" />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-xml-attr>
																<do-for-each>

																		<token-xpath expression="$filter/filter/filter-class[@class-name=@class-name]/filter-attr[@subscriber='sync' or @subscriber='notify']/@attr-name" />
																	</arg-node-set>
																	<arg-actions>
																		<do-set-local-variable name="value" scope="policy">
																			<arg-node-set>
																				<token-attr name="$current-node$" />
																			</arg-node-set>
																		</do-set-local-variable>

																						<token-text xml:space="preserve">fanout</token-text>

																			</arg-actions>
																			<arg-actions />

																</do-for-each>
																<do-for-each>
																	<arg-node-set>
																		<token-xpath expression="../add[last()]/add-attr[@attr-name='urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:ilm:static:1.0:User:dirXMLEntitlementRef']/value" />

This rule performs error recovery for fanout operations on associated objects based on existing UserAccount entitlements. It triggers when the UserAccount entitlement GCV is true, an association exists, and the UserAccount entitlement is not changing. The rule extracts the local system name (lsname) from the association, then iterates through all UserAccount entitlements to find systems that should have received fanout events but didn't (checking for missing associations and nodes). For each missing fanout, it reconstructs an add event by cloning the driver's filter attributes, adjusting entitlement references to only include those relevant to the target system, and setting appropriate operation-data attributes. It also handles CUA (Consolidated User Administration) child systems specially by managing entitlement references. Finally, it strips entitlement references that don't belong to the current system from all operations and removes empty attribute modifications.

content.text:
Fix the syntax errors in this DirXML policy based on the DTD.

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Strip Login Disabled from operation (RACFAccount Entitlement but NO Onboarding)</description>
	<comment xml:space="preserve">If entitlements control whether the account in the application is enabled or disabled (as in the Disable Option), we'll disregard changes to Login Disabled.
If RACFAccount onboarding is allowed we will strip the attribute in the pub-ctp-PermissionAttributesCaching policy</comment>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">disable</if-global-variable>
			<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
			<if-op-attr name="Login Disabled" op="available" />
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount.onboard" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-strip-op-attr name="Login Disabled" />
	</actions>
</rule>

The original XML violates the DirXML DTD by having two <and> elements as direct children of <conditions>. According to the schema, <conditions> can only contain a single boolean logic container (like <and>, <or>, or a single condition). The two <and> blocks create an implicit OR relationship, but this must be explicitly structured. To fix this, I wrapped both <and> blocks in an <or> container, making the logic explicit: (condition_set_1 AND all_its_conditions) OR (condition_set_2 AND all_its_conditions). Alternatively, since both condition sets are nearly identical except for one variable name, I created a simpler corrected version with a single <and> block that checks both onboarding variables within it, which is logically equivalent and cleaner.

Corrected XML:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
	<description>Strip Login Disabled from operation (RACFAccount Entitlement but NO Onboarding)</description>
	<comment xml:space="preserve">If entitlements control whether the account in the application is enabled or disabled (as in the Disable Option), we'll disregard changes to Login Disabled.
If RACFAccount onboarding is allowed we will strip the attribute in the pub-ctp-PermissionAttributesCaching policy</comment>
	<conditions>
		<and>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable name="drv.entitlement.remove" op="equal">disable</if-global-variable>
			<if-class-name op="equal">User</if-class-name>
			<if-op-attr name="Login Disabled" op="available" />
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.RACFAccount.onboard" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
			<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="not-equal">true</if-global-variable>
		</and>
	</conditions>
	<actions>
		<do-strip-op-attr name="Login Disabled" />
	</actions>
</rule>

[Context/Input]:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>process rename operation (with copyTo and Delete option)</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.role.rename.option" op="equal">2</if-global-variable>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.role.copyto.option" op="equal">2</if-global-variable>
											<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="lvCopyTo" op="equal">0</if-local-variable>
										</and>
									</conditions>
									<actions>
										<do-delete-dest-object class-name="US" when="after">
											<arg-association>
												<token-local-variable name="lvAss" />
											</arg-association>
										</do-delete-dest-object>
										<do-set-local-variable name="lvTmp" scope="policy">
											<arg-string>
												<token-text xml:space="preserve">Delete SAP object </token-text>
												<token-local-variable name="lvDestDN" />
											</arg-string>
										</do-set-local-variable>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule handles a rename operation using a copy-and-delete strategy. It checks three conditions: (1) the global rename option is set to '2', (2) the global copyTo option is set to '2', and (3) the local variable 'lvCopyTo' equals '0'. When all conditions are met, it deletes the destination object of class 'US' using the association stored in local variable 'lvAss', scheduling the deletion to occur 'after' the current operation. It then sets a local variable 'lvTmp' with a descriptive message indicating which SAP object was deleted, concatenating the text 'Delete SAP object ' with the destination DN from the 'lvDestDN' local variable.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Acquire mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">Each IDM driver has two threads: the subscriber and the publisher thread. Both threads might be manipulating the same data, in this case the DRVR__CACHE driver scope variable. To avoid cache corruption, the policy acquires a mutex before manipulating or reading the cache and releases the mutex when done. If the policy finds the mutex unavailable, that means that the same policy has been invoked by the other thread and has to finish its job, before the policy on the current thread can continue. The mutex is another driver scope vairable DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX.</comment>
									<conditions />
									<actions>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-trace-message>
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-trace-message>
												<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-if>
													<arg-conditions>
														<and>
															<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
														</and>
													</arg-conditions>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-trace-message>
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-trace-message>
														<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-if>
															<arg-conditions>
																<and>
																	<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
																</and>
															</arg-conditions>
															<arg-actions>
																<do-trace-message>
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
																	</arg-string>
																</do-trace-message>
																<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-local-variable>
															</arg-actions>
															<arg-actions />
														</do-if>
													</arg-actions>
													<arg-actions />
												</do-if>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions />
										</do-if>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX" op="not-equal">true</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX" scope="driver">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">true</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-trace-message>
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Successfully acquired mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX.</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-trace-message>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-status level="error">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Unable to acquire mutex DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX. Aborting DRVR__CACHE refresh/initialization.</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-status>
												<do-break />
											</arg-actions>
										</do-if>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule implements a mutex acquisition mechanism for thread-safe cache access in NetIQ DirXML. It checks if the driver-scope variable DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX is available (not set to 'true'). If the mutex is locked, it waits 1 second and retries up to three times (nested do-if statements). After the retry attempts, if the mutex is available (not equal to 'true'), it sets DRVR__CACHE__MUTEX to 'true' to acquire the lock and logs success. If still unavailable after retries, it returns an error status and breaks execution. This prevents race conditions when both subscriber and publisher threads access the DRVR__CACHE variable simultaneously.

											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="regex" name="eventId" op="equal">.*__Scim.*</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>

											<arg-actions />

This rule vetoes (blocks) loopback events in a NetIQ DirXML/Identity Manager driver. It first checks if the event has an event-id attribute and if the operation is either 'add' or 'modify'. If these conditions are met, it extracts the event-id into a local variable called 'eventId'. Then it performs a regex match to check if the eventId contains '__Scim' anywhere in its value. If this pattern matches, the event is vetoed to prevent processing, effectively blocking SCIM-originated events from looping back through the system.

The broken XML removed the 'before' and 'expression' attributes from the <do-append-xml-element> action, which violates the DTD requirement that do-append-xml-element must specify where to append (expression attribute for the parent context) and optionally positioning (before attribute). Without 'expression', the engine doesn't know which element to append to, and without 'before', it doesn't know the insertion point relative to sibling elements. The corrected version restores both attributes: expression='modify-attr' specifies the parent element context, and before='add-value' ensures the remove-all-values element is inserted before any add-value siblings.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rule>
									<description>Acquire mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX</description>
									<comment xml:space="preserve">Each IDM driver has two threads: the subscriber and the publisher thread. Both threads might be manipulating the same data, in this case the RULE__CACHE driver scope variable. To avoid cache corruption, the policy acquires a mutex before manipulating or reading the cache and releases the mutex when done. If the policy finds the mutex unavailable, that means that the same policy has been invoked by the other thread and has to finish its job, before the policy on the current thread can continue. The mutex is another driver scope vairable RULE__CACHE__MUTEX.</comment>
									<conditions />
									<actions>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="RULE__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-trace-message>
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-trace-message>
												<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
													<arg-string>
														<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-if>
													<arg-conditions>
														<and>
															<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="RULE__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
														</and>
													</arg-conditions>
													<arg-actions>
														<do-trace-message>
															<arg-string>
																<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
															</arg-string>
														</do-trace-message>
														<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
															<arg-string>
																<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
															</arg-string>
														</do-set-local-variable>
														<do-if>
															<arg-conditions>
																<and>
																	<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="RULE__CACHE__MUTEX" op="equal">true</if-local-variable>
																</and>
															</arg-conditions>
															<arg-actions>
																<do-trace-message>
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-text xml:space="preserve">Mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX not available. Retrying in 1 second...</token-text>
																	</arg-string>
																</do-trace-message>
																<do-set-local-variable name="tmp" scope="policy">
																	<arg-string>
																		<token-xpath expression="es:doWait('1000')" />
																	</arg-string>
																</do-set-local-variable>
															</arg-actions>
															<arg-actions />
														</do-if>
													</arg-actions>
													<arg-actions />
												</do-if>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions />
										</do-if>
										<do-if>
											<arg-conditions>
												<and>
													<if-local-variable mode="nocase" name="RULE__CACHE__MUTEX" op="not-equal">true</if-local-variable>
												</and>
											</arg-conditions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-set-local-variable name="RULE__CACHE__MUTEX" scope="driver">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">true</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-set-local-variable>
												<do-trace-message>
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Successfully acquired mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX.</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-trace-message>
											</arg-actions>
											<arg-actions>
												<do-status level="error">
													<arg-string>
														<token-text xml:space="preserve">Unable to acquire mutex RULE__CACHE__MUTEX. Aborting RULE__CACHE refresh/initialization.</token-text>
													</arg-string>
												</do-status>
												<do-break />
											</arg-actions>
										</do-if>
									</actions>
								</rule>

This rule implements a mutex locking mechanism for thread-safe cache access in a NetIQ IDM driver. It attempts to acquire a mutex (RULE__CACHE__MUTEX) by checking if it's available (not equal to 'true'). If the mutex is already held, it retries up to 3 times with 1-second waits between attempts using the es:doWait() extension function. After the retry attempts, if the mutex is still unavailable, it logs an error and aborts. If successful, it sets the mutex variable to 'true' at driver scope and logs success. The mutex prevents cache corruption when both subscriber and publisher threads access the RULE__CACHE driver scope variable simultaneously.

<rule>
									<description>Remove ALL entitlements if account deleted</description>
									<conditions>
										<and>
											<if-operation mode="case" op="equal">delete</if-operation>
											<if-class-name mode="nocase" op="equal">User</if-class-name>
											<if-global-variable mode="nocase" name="drv.entitlement.onboarding" op="equal">true</if-global-variable>
